title: LGGR derivation DAG (first pass)
description: Claims derived from examples/, cookbooks/, code/, lean4/ and workflows/ (first pass, 2026-11-14). Claims from atlas/archive/papers/ are a later phase. Every node has exactly one status; statuses are never raised without replayed evidence.

statuses.PROVED_LEAN: A named Lean 4 theorem states the claim (within the stated scope) and the lean4/ package builds with zero sorry.
statuses.TESTED_RUST: Checked by a named Rust test in code/rust on the stated finite instances; no general proof in this repository.
statuses.EMPIRICAL: Measured in a recorded workflow run; not a theorem.
statuses.OPEN: A goal; neither proved nor tested.

claim_correspondence.AUTHOR_MATCHED: The ledger statement was written against the cited Lean theorem by the author of this pass; not independently reviewed, and not machine-checked against the theorem type.
claim_correspondence.DOCSTRING_ONLY: The statement is the Lean docstring; the theorem type itself was not compared.
claim_correspondence.REVIEWED: An independent reviewer compared the ledger statement with the theorem type.

proof_existence_vs_correspondence: PROVED_LEAN means a cited theorem exists and the package builds with zero sorry (checked in CI). Whether the theorem says what the ledger says is tracked separately in claim_correspondence.

nodes.title: A collision refutes every decoder
nodes.statement: If p(x) = p(y) and q(x) != q(y), no map D with D(p(z)) = q(z) for all z exists.
nodes.scope: general

nodes.title: Decoder-or-collision dichotomy on a finite table
nodes.statement: On a supplied finite table, exactly one holds: q is constant on every realized fiber of p (and the fiberwise decoder replays on every row), or an explicit colliding pair exists.
nodes.scope: finite tables; exhaustive census of all 216 maps p:{3}->{3}, q:{3}->{2}
nodes.notes: The decoder direction is proved in Lean only as the classical pair-level alternative in WorldLGGRWitness (uses Classical.choice, no executable search). The general finite-table dichotomy is checked by exhaustive Rust census, not proved for all finite carriers.

nodes.title: Postprocessing preserves collisions
nodes.statement: For any deterministic f : A -> A', a collision of (p, q) is a collision of (f o p, q); postprocessing cannot restore a decoder.
nodes.scope: general

nodes.title: Verdict ceiling on a colliding pair
nodes.statement: Any report-only evaluator E : A -> B disagrees with q on at least one member of a colliding pair.
nodes.scope: general

nodes.title: Boolean evaluator defect partition
nodes.statement: Delta_E = E_g - E_1 E_2 takes values in {-1, 0, 1}, and Delta_E = -1 (NGD, local green / global red) exactly at (E_1, E_2, E_g) = (1, 1, 0).
nodes.scope: general (all 8 Boolean triples)

nodes.title: Metadata refinement removes a collision
nodes.statement: If x, y collide under p and a feature m has m(x) != m(y), then x, y do not collide under z -> (p(z), m(z)).
nodes.scope: general

nodes.title: Online collision monotonicity
nodes.statement: A report-fiber collision present in a trace persists in every extension of the trace; an online monitor's collision verdict never retracts.
nodes.scope: general

nodes.title: Boundary-sufficient gluing gives zero defect (composable LGGG)
nodes.statement: If the boundary summaries are sufficient (E_g = E_1 and E_2) and every local stage passes, the global check passes and Delta_E = 0.
nodes.scope: general

nodes.title: Boundary insufficiency forces NGD
nodes.statement: If two locally passing traces share a report but disagree on the global oracle, at least one branch has Delta_E = -1.
nodes.scope: general

nodes.title: Signed increments telescope
nodes.statement: For any history x_0, ..., x_n, the sum of signed steps equals x_n - x_0.
nodes.scope: general (Lean: streaming_chain_telescoping over lists)

nodes.title: Local step bounds do not imply the endpoint bound
nodes.statement: With B = 1, the history (0, 1, 2) has every |dx_i| <= 1 but |x_2 - x_0| = 2 > 1.
nodes.scope: instance (0,1,2), B = 1

nodes.title: Every-prefix boundedness is strictly stronger than endpoint boundedness
nodes.statement: Every-prefix boundedness implies endpoint boundedness; (0, 1, 2, 1) with B = 1 is endpoint-bounded but not prefix-bounded.
nodes.scope: implication general; separation on the instance (0,1,2,1)

nodes.title: Unsigned step reports collide; signed reports separate
nodes.statement: (0, 1, 0) and (0, 1, 2) have the same unsigned step report (1, 1) but different endpoint verdicts; the signed report separates them.
nodes.scope: instance

nodes.title: Prefix violations latch (online early stopping is sound)
nodes.statement: Once a prefix exceeds the bound, no extension restores prefix admissibility, so stopping at the first excursion loses nothing.
nodes.scope: general

nodes.title: The audit keeps five outcomes separate
nodes.statement: On the example histories the audit returns COMPOSITION_VERIFIED (good), OBSTRUCTION_DETECTED (bad: signed total 2 > 1), WITNESS_INCOMPLETE (reports only: missing endpoints), WITNESS_INCOMPLETE (open obligation retained) and AUTHORITY_REQUIRED (changed authority id).
nodes.scope: the five supplied example documents
nodes.notes: A replay of the finite budget model on supplied data; not runtime or merge authorization.

nodes.title: Recorded policy digests replay
nodes.statement: Every witness's policy_sha256 equals SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the example policy.
nodes.scope: the five supplied example documents
nodes.notes: A digest binds data; it does not establish truth or grant authority.

nodes.title: Weighted-l1 weak duality certificate
nodes.statement: If D^T z = 0 and |z_e| <= w_e, then z.h <= sum_e w_e |h_e - (Dx)_e| for every x; equality certifies the optimum, and z.h > 0 certifies that h is not repairable.
nodes.scope: checked on the triangle over a grid of potentials; general statement is prose
nodes.notes: Weak duality holds in general (one-line triangle inequality); no general Lean theorem in this repository yet.

nodes.title: Triangle l1 primal/dual optimality
nodes.statement: For D_0 the triangle coboundary and h = (1, 1, 1), z = (1, 1, -1) and x = (0, 1, 2) certify min_x ||h - D_0 x||_1 = 1.
nodes.scope: instance

nodes.title: Filled triangle: closure failure vs budget exactness
nodes.scope: instance

nodes.title: Cycle closure: nonzero circulation is an obstruction, certified by a cycle-flow dual
nodes.statement: When a streamed edge closes a cycle with defect d = h_e - (x_v - x_u) != 0, the cochain is not exact; on the unfilled triangle (1, 1, 1) is closed but not exact (nonzero H^1). For one fundamental cycle the weighted-l1 repair distance is |d| times the minimum weight on the cycle.
nodes.scope: Lean: integer circulation instance (residual >= 1) and the 4-vertex complex; Rust: monitor instances incl. cookbook 03 (defect 3, distance 3)
nodes.notes: The weighted min-weight formula is checked in Rust on instances; Lean covers the unit-weight residual bound.

nodes.title: Open chains are exact
nodes.statement: A streamed acyclic (tree) family of 1-cochains has zero circulation and is a coboundary.
nodes.scope: Lean: two-edge chain; Rust: tree instance

nodes.title: A chain retraction reflects repair and obstruction
nodes.statement: If F commutes with the coboundaries and G is a left-inverse chain map (G_1 D_T = D_S G_0, G F = I), target repairs pull back and source nonrepairability is reflected.
nodes.scope: general

nodes.title: A lossy projection cannot reflect nonrepairability
nodes.statement: A non-injective projection admits no left inverse; dropping the chord sends the exact (1,1,2) and the frustrated (1,1,1) to the same repairable image (1,1).
nodes.scope: general (non-injectivity) plus the chord-drop instance

nodes.title: Two-point fiber minimax lower bound (integer predictors)
nodes.statement: On a fiber with integer target values a <= b, every integer prediction z has 2 max(|a - z|, |b - z|) >= b - a, with equality at m when a + b = 2m for an integer m.
nodes.scope: lower bound for every integer z; attainment only under the hypothesis a + b = 2m (m an integer)
nodes.notes: Rescoped 2026-11-14 after review: the theorem does not cover odd a + b; see LGGR-C37.

nodes.title: Integer two-point optimum is the ceiling
nodes.statement: Over integer predictors, min_z max(|a - z|, |b - z|) = ceil((b - a)/2). When a + b is odd (e.g. a = 0, b = 1, optimum 1) the value (b - a)/2 is reached only by a rational predictor.
nodes.scope: exhaustive for -5 <= a <= b <= 5
nodes.notes: Added 2026-11-14 from review finding 3. Not yet in Lean.

nodes.title: General fiber minimax floor on a finite table
nodes.statement: For O : H -> Y and integer f : H -> Z, over rational predictors g : Y -> Q, inf_g max_h |f(h) - g(O(h))| = (1/2) max_y W_f(y), attained by the fiber midpoint (which may be a half-integer). Every integer-valued predictor is bounded below by the same value.
nodes.scope: exhaustive over all 3-history tables with binary observations and targets in {-2..2}
nodes.notes: Rust checks the lower bound over integer predictors and attainment by the rational midpoint (in doubled units). General multi-point statement is not yet in Lean.

nodes.title: Evidence-preserving recursion keeps the floor
nodes.statement: Any finite chain of self-updates that sees only the fixed evidence y = O(h) yields one output per fiber, so its worst-case error stays >= W_f(y)/2.
nodes.scope: Lean: two update operators on a colliding pair; Rust: composed update instances
nodes.notes: Deterministic updates only in the Rust check; the randomized statement in the README is prose.

nodes.title: CHSH local bound and PR-box violation
nodes.statement: Every deterministic local strategy has |S| = 2, so every local behaviour has |S| <= 2; the PR box has S = 4.
nodes.scope: general for the 16 deterministic vertices

nodes.title: Pairwise-compatible odd cycle has no global section
nodes.statement: Constraints x_i != x_{i+1} around an odd cycle are satisfiable on every edge and every proper path, yet no global assignment exists (local green, global red); even cycles glue.
nodes.scope: Lean: 3-cycle marginal invariant; Rust: n = 3, 5, 7

nodes.title: Mermin-Peres parity obstruction
nodes.statement: Every row and column context of the magic square is satisfiable, but no global +/-1 assignment meets row products (1,1,1) and column products (1,1,-1).
nodes.scope: general (finite)

nodes.title: Contextual-fraction packing bound (scaled arithmetic)
nodes.statement: With constant context weight m, U = S + N and R = mN give U - R = S - (m - 1)N, so any packing Gamma >= U - R has S - Gamma <= (m - 1)N, the scaled form of CF <= (m - 1) N_min.
nodes.scope: the arithmetic step; the LP reading CF <= (m-1) N_min is prose
nodes.notes: The Lean theorem assumes the mass identities U = S + N and R = mN; their derivation from an LP signed extension is not formalized here.

nodes.title: Three-party separation CF(p*) > 2 N_min(p*) (arithmetic on supplied optima)
nodes.statement: Given optimal packing mass 540/768 and negative mass 75/768 at p* (GHZ rnd2), CF(p*) = 19/64 and N_min(p*) = 25/256, so CF - 2 N_min = 13/128 > 0, and the order reverses against Q_{5/8}.
nodes.scope: arithmetic over denominator 768 on supplied optima
nodes.notes: Optimality of 540/768 and 75/768 (the LP primal/dual certificates) is not checked in Lean or Rust in this repository; see LGGR-O04.

nodes.title: Host elimination rule: no false accept in model
nodes.statement: If the true hypothesis is in the declared space and every observation is faithful, the host rule (accept iff every surviving hypothesis passes) never accepts a failing system and never rejects a passing one.
nodes.scope: exhaustive over 3-hypothesis, 2-check spaces; general proof is one line (the truth survives elimination)

nodes.title: Out of model, the host rule can false-accept
nodes.statement: If the true world lies outside the hypothesis space, evidence consistent with only passing hypotheses makes the host accept a failing system.
nodes.scope: explicit counterexample

nodes.title: The LGGR selector quantity vanishes exactly at resolution
nodes.statement: The number of surviving accept/reject hypothesis pairs is zero if and only if the host rule is resolved (all survivors agree).
nodes.scope: exhaustive over 4-hypothesis spaces

nodes.title: cross branch audit splice budget breach
nodes.statement: Theorem 17 (`cross_branch_audit_splice_budget_breach`): Two stage traces with cumulative deltas `d1` and `d2` can each satisfy the budget bound `|d1| ≤ B` and `|d2| ≤ B` in isolation (`COMPOSABLE_LGGG`), while their spliced composition has cumulative delta `d1 + d2` violating `|d1 + d2| > B` (`cross_branch_lggr_discovered`).

nodes.title: multi stage gluing associativity and defect bound
nodes.statement: Theorem 18 (`multi_stage_gluing_associativity_and_defect_bound`): 1. (Associativity of G2 Signed Delta & Multiplicative Local Acceptance): Across three stages with signed deltas `(d1, d2, d3)` and local acceptance bits `(e1, e2, e3)`, both `(d1 + d2) + d3 = d1 + (d2 + d3)` and `(e1 && e2) && e3 = e1 && (e2 && e3)` hold. 2. (Non-Associativity of Thresholded Budget Gluing): For budget threshold `B = 2` and stage deltas `(2, 2, -2)`, grouping `d1 + (d2 + d3)` yields intermediate sum `|2 + (-2)| = 0 ≤ 2` and total `|2 + 0| = 2 ≤ 2`, whereas the left-prefix grouping `(d1 + d2) + d3` hits intermediate prefix `|2 + 2| = 4 > 2`.

nodes.title: coarsened macro stage masks internal prefix breach
nodes.statement: Theorem 19 (`coarsened_macro_stage_masks_internal_prefix_breach`): For a 3-step state trajectory `x0 → x1 → x2 → x3` with cumulative budget `B`, coarsening steps 2 and 3 into a single macro-step `x1 → x3` checks only `|x1 - x0| ≤ B` and `|x3 - x0| ≤ B`. Every fine-grained prefix-bounded trajectory satisfies the coarsened check, whereas the trajectory `(0, 1, 3, 1)` with `B = 2` passes the coarsened check (`|1 - 0| ≤ 2` and `|1 - 0| ≤ 2`) while violating the internal prefix `|3 - 0| = 3 > 2`.

nodes.title: deferred obligation and scope migration separation
nodes.statement: Theorem 21 (`deferred_obligation_and_scope_migration_separation`): 1. (Obligation Retention Monotonicity): For non-negative step obligation counts `o1 ≥ 1` and `o2 ≥ 0`, the cumulative retained obligation count `o1 + o2 ≥ 1` remains strictly positive even when the subsequent step introduces zero new obligations (`o2 = 0`). 2. (Strict Soundness Refinement & False-Acceptance Separation): Full LGGR acceptance implies conventional local+endpoint acceptance, whereas mid-flight prefix breaches (`prefix_ok = false`), silent representation/scope migrations (`scope_ok = false`), or unresolved deferred obligations (`obligations_clear = false`) cause conventional false acceptance (`conventionalAccepts = true` while `lggrFullAccepts = false`).

nodes.title: l1 dual witness subgradient weight sensitivity
nodes.statement: Theorem 22 (`l1_dual_witness_subgradient_weight_sensitivity`): 1. (Dual Feasibility Under Non-Negative Weight Increases): If a dual witness `(z1, z2, z3)` satisfies `|zi| ≤ wi` and weight increments satisfy `dwi ≥ 0`, then `|zi| ≤ wi + dwi`. 2. (Monotonicity of Weighted L1 Residual): For any residual vector `(r1, r2, r3)` and non-negative weight increments `dw1, dw2, dw3 ≥ 0`, the weighted L1 cost satisfies `weightedL1Cost3 (w1 + dw1) (w2 + dw2) (w3 + dw3) r1 r2 r3 - weightedL1Cost3 w1 w2 w3 r1 r2 r3 = dw1 * |r1| + dw2 * |r2| + dw3 * |r3| ≥ 0`.

nodes.title: cycle bottleneck weight pivot threshold
nodes.statement: Theorem 23 (`cycle_bottleneck_weight_pivot_threshold`): Consider a frustrated cycle (or coupled cycle cut) with nonzero defect magnitude `d > 0`, where breaking the active chord `e` incurs cost `w_e * d` while breaking the alternative tree cut incurs cost `C_alt * d`: 1. Below the critical weight (`w_e < C_alt`), breaking `e` is strictly cheaper (`w_e * d < C_alt * d`), 2. At the critical weight (`w_e = C_alt`), both bases achieve identical repair cost (`w_e * d = C_alt * d`), 3. Above the critical weight (`w_e > C_alt`), pivoting `e` into the spanning tree and breaking the alternative cut is strictly cheaper (`C_alt * d < w_e * d`).
nodes.scope: as stated in the Lean theorem
nodes.notes: Not yet curated into a core claim; extracted from the Lean source.

nodes.title: six role sample defect and cancellation masking
nodes.statement: Theorem 24 (`six_role_sample_defect_and_cancellation_masking`): Formalizes the LGGR III Six-Role Overlay finite sample laws: 1. (Sample Global-Minus-Local Identity): Across any two role-evaluated triples `(e1a, e2a, ega)` and `(e1b, e2b, egb)`, the global sum minus local-product sum equals the sum of signed defects: `(ega + egb) - (e1a * e2a + e1b * e2b) = roleTripleDefect e1a e2a ega + roleTripleDefect e1b e2b egb`. 2. (Signed Cancellation Masking): For the PGD triple `(0, 1, 1)` (`Δ_E = +1`) and the NGD triple `(1, 1, 0)` (`Δ_E = -1`), the signed defect sum vanishes (`D = 0`) while the disagreement count `M = |Δ_E(v1)| + |Δ_E(v2)| = 2 > 0` detects the masked NGD failure. 3. (Observation Envelope Separation): For any positive residual `R > 0` and distinct envelope weights `w1 ≠ w2`, `w1 * R ≠ w2 * R`.

nodes.title: completion relative obstruction on carrier extension
nodes.statement: Theorem 25 (`completion_relative_obstruction_on_carrier_extension`): Formalizes the LGGR IV Completion-Relative Obstruction (Finite-Stage Green + Projective Thread Compatibility + Original-Carrier Integer Obstruction): 1. (Finite-Stage Solvability): For stages `n = 1, 2, 3, 4` with moduli `2, 4, 8, 16`, the witnesses `x1 = -1, x2 = 1, x3 = -3, x4 = 5` satisfy `(3 * xn + 1) % 2^n = 0`. 2. (Projective Thread Compatibility): Adjacent stage witnesses agree modulo the coarser stage modulus: `(x2 - x1) % 2 = 0`, `(x3 - x2) % 4 = 0`, `(x4 - x3) % 8 = 0`. 3. (Original-Carrier Integer Obstruction): No integer `x : Int` in the original carrier satisfies the completed equation `3 * x + 1 = 0`.

nodes.title: disjoint colliding pairs additive error lower bound
nodes.statement: Theorem 26 (`disjoint_colliding_pairs_additive_error_lower_bound`): Formalizes the LGGR I / V / VI Disjoint Colliding-Pairs Additive Error Ceiling and Post-Processing Invariance: 1. Across any two colliding pairs `(x1, y1)` and `(x2, y2)`, any deterministic report-only predictor `E : A → B` incurs at least `2` classification errors: `(err(x1) + err(y1)) + (err(x2) + err(y2)) ≥ 2`. 2. For any deterministic post-processing map `f : A → A'` and downstream predictor `E' : A' → B`, the post-processed predictor `E' ∘ f ∘ p` obeys the same additive error lower bound `≥ 2`.

nodes.title: centered gram kernel nullspace obstruction
nodes.statement: Theorem 27 (`centered_gram_kernel_nullspace_obstruction`): Formalizes the LGGR VI Gram Kernel Identity, Hidden Nullspace Blindspot, and Sign-Cube Adjoint Probe Recovery: 1. (Gram Kernel Identity & Nullspace Blindspot): For `Q0(x1, x2) = x1` and `H0(x1, x2) = Q0^T Q0 (x1, x2) = (x1, 0)`, `H0(x1, x2) = (0, 0) ↔ Q0(x1, x2) = 0`, and every nonzero vertical state `(0, t)` (`t ≠ 0`) produces zero observation and zero Gram response (`Q0(0, t) = 0 ∧ H0(0, t) = (0, 0)`). 2. (Zero-Preserving Post-Processing Blindness): Any post-processor `A : Int → V` applied to `Q0` assigns the same verdict to any hidden state `(0, t)` as to `(0, 0)`: `A (projQ0 0 t) = A (projQ0 0 0)`. 3. (Full 2D Sign-Cube Recovery): Across the `2^2 = 4` corners of `{-1, +1}^2`, `(signCubeSum1 g1 g2, signCubeSum2 g1 g2) = (4 * g1, 4 * g2)`.

nodes.title: path kernel composition discrepancy identity
nodes.statement: Theorem 28 (`path_kernel_composition_discrepancy_identity`): Formalizes the LGGR I / III Evaluated Path-Kernel Composition & Two-Channel Residual Identity: 1. (Two-Channel Four-Term Expansion): For any local product `L`, global verdict `Eg`, factored weight `wProd`, global weight `wg`, evaluator defect `dE = Eg - L`, and weight defect `dw = wg - wProd`, `Eg * wg = L * wProd + dE * wProd + L * dw + dE * dw`. 2. (Two-Slice Evaluated Kernel Discrepancy): Across two boundary slices `a` and `b` with factored path weights `wa, wb` and defects `dEa = Ega - La`, `dEb = Egb - Lb`, `(Ega * wa + Egb * wb) - (La * wa + Lb * wb) = dEa * wa + dEb * wb`.

nodes.title: boundary sufficiency without quotient factorization
nodes.statement: Theorem 29 (`boundary_sufficiency_without_quotient_factorization`): Formalizes the LGGR II Organizational Gluing laws (Claims M3, M4, M5, M9): 1. (Product Sufficiency Equivalence — M4): Under weak sufficiency (`r3 = eg`), product sufficiency (`r3 = e1 * e2`) holds if and only if `eg = e1 * e2`. 2. (Weak Sufficiency Without Factorization — M3): For `(e1, e2, eg, r3) = (1, 1, 0, 0)`, weak sufficiency (`r3 = eg`) holds while `roleTripleDefect 1 1 0 = -1 ≠ 0`. 3. (Scalar Defect Non-Additivity — M5): Three NGD defects `(-1) + (-1) + (-1) = -3` leave the legal defect range `{-1, 0, 1}`. 4. (Carrier-Local Transport Forces NGD on Mixed Class — M9): If two traces share a locally passing joint carrier (`l1 = true ∧ l2 = true`) and have opposite global verdicts (`eg1 ≠ eg2`), at least one trace has `streamingEvalDefect = -1` (NGD).

nodes.title: realizable defect soundness kernel intersection
nodes.statement: Theorem 30 (`realizable_defect_soundness_kernel_intersection`): Explicit integer defect-vector, coupled-coordinate, and Minkowski fixtures from LGGR V.
